sites.name: Tombs of the Old Kings
sites.text: Weathered vaults cut into the Apennine foothills, older than any road that passes them.

outcomes.text: The vaults are long since picked over, but a sealed niche yields a pouch of worn coin.
Your soldiers spend a wary night among the dead and come out steadier for it.
Behind a fallen slab: grave-gold the robbers never found.

sites.name: Spring of the Twins
sites.text: A cold spring under a fig tree, where herdsmen leave offerings to two nameless brothers.

outcomes.text: The men drink, make their offerings, and march away believing themselves favored.
Among the offerings lies more silver than piety strictly requires.
The keeper of the spring blesses the column and presses the shrine's tithe-box on its commander.

sites.name: Smugglers' Cove
sites.text: A sea-cave below the cliffs that the fishermen swear they have never once entered.

outcomes.text: Oil, wine, and a strongbox of coin, abandoned in haste.
The smugglers' whole season's takings, still crated for shipment.
Behind a false wall, the cove's true hoard — years of untaxed profit.

sites.name: Hillside Deserters
sites.text: Campfires in the high country: soldiers of some beaten army, living lean and unclaimed.

outcomes.text: A band of them takes your salt and your standard.
Two full companies march down from the hills to join you.
The camp is abandoned — but they left their loot behind.

sites.name: Sanctuary of the Sea God
sites.text: Salt-eaten columns above the western strand, half-buried in dune.

outcomes.text: Votive silver glints in the sand between the fallen stones.
The men clear the old altar and sacrifice before it; the sea wind feels kinder after.
A temple cellar, dry and sealed, stacked with dedicated treasure.

sites.name: Abandoned River Fort
sites.text: A palisaded post above the Po crossings, its gate swinging open to the wind.

outcomes.text: The paymaster's chest was too heavy to carry off in whatever hurry emptied this place.
Your soldiers drill in the old yard and study how the walls were laid.
Under the granary floor, the garrison's buried savings.

sites.name: Wreckers' Hoard
sites.text: Coastal folk here light false beacons on stormy nights. Somewhere they keep what the sea delivers.

outcomes.text: A cave stacked with salvage: amphorae, bronze fittings, and coin.
The wreckers' shares, counted and bagged for a division that never came.
A drowned merchantman's strongroom, hauled ashore whole.

sites.name: Oracle of the Salt Pans
sites.text: A lone priestess keeps a smoking altar where the salt flats shimmer like water.

outcomes.text: She reads the smoke and names your soldiers fortunate; they choose to believe her.
Pilgrims' offerings have piled up faster than one priestess can spend them.
The priestess anoints the column's standard and opens the shrine's coffer in tribute.

sites.name: The Painted Colonnade
sites.text: A hillside portico burned in some old war, its frescoes fading under the soot.

outcomes.text: Beneath a collapsed wall, a householder's strongbox nobody came back for.
An old soldier squatting in the ruin drills your officers in the deeds painted on the walls.
A bronze horde buried at the colonnade's foot, green with age and heavy with worth.

sites.name: The Warrior's Cenotaph
sites.text: An empty tomb raised for a champion whose body was never brought home.

outcomes.text: Your soldiers stand a silent watch at the stone and carry its weight away with them.
Grave-offerings of silver lie untouched — until now.
The dead man's kin still keep the tomb; they arm your officers and fill their purses in his name.

sites.name: Royal Hunting Lodge
sites.text: A king's lodge gone to bramble, its trophy hall open to the sky.

outcomes.text: Silver plate, tarnished but whole, still on the feasting boards.
The old huntsmen's paths make a hard day's exercise for the column.
The king's private strongroom, its lock long rusted to nothing.

sites.name: The Pirate King's Cache
sites.text: Every sailor on this coast tells of a raider-lord who buried his takings and died before spending them.

outcomes.text: A tar-sealed chest under a lightning-split pine — part of the legend is true.
Two chests, and the second heavier than the first.
The whole hoard, ship's ransom upon ship's ransom.

sites.name: Sunken Delta Temple
sites.text: Pylons leaning out of the marsh where a branch of the river changed its mind a century ago.

outcomes.text: Waterlogged offering-chests, their contents better preserved than their carriers hoped.
Wading the flooded halls in battle order is a drill the men never forget.
A priest's treasury above the waterline, untouched behind a jackal-headed seal.

sites.name: Quarry Masters' Vault
sites.text: The old quarry offices above the cataracts, sealed when the granite ran out.

outcomes.text: Wage-silver for a workforce that was never paid off.
The masters' ledger and the strongbox it accounts for.
A vault of temple commissions, paid in advance and never delivered.

sites.name: Caravan Beacon Tower
sites.text: A signal tower on the desert road, dark since its keepers stopped being paid.

outcomes.text: Toll-money still in the counting room, in a dozen currencies.
From the tower top your scouts learn to read the desert roads like a ledger.
A merchant prince's deposit, left for safekeeping with keepers who kept nothing else.

sites.name: Ziggurat of the Moon
sites.text: A stepped mountain of brick outside the irrigated land, its stairs worn to ramps.

outcomes.text: Foundation deposits of silver, laid down when the bricks were new.
The climb in full kit, twice, at noon. The men curse you and grow harder.
A star-priests' cache in the summit shrine, meant to outlast an eclipse of the world.

sites.name: Mountain Deserters
sites.text: Smoke in the high passes: hired spears who walked away from someone's war.

outcomes.text: A company of them prefers your wages to the winter.
Their whole camp musters under your banner by nightfall.
Gone — over the pass ahead of the snow. Their cache was too heavy to take.

sites.name: Silk Road Waystation
sites.text: A caravanserai on the eastern road, shuttered mid-season with the stables still full of straw.

outcomes.text: A merchant's deposit-chest behind the well.
Bales of silk bricked into a dry cistern, worth more than their weight in argument.
The stationmaster's secret: a season of skimmed tolls in gold.

sites.name: Grove of the Speaking Oak
sites.text: An oak older than the tribes, hung with offerings, where the wind is said to answer questions.

outcomes.text: Whatever the wind said, the men march out of the grove certain of themselves.
Among the hung offerings: torcs and coin enough to fill a pay-chest.
The grove-keeper reads the leaves for your commander and gifts the column the shrine's portion.

sites.name: Tin Traders' Hideaway
sites.text: A fortified beach-house where the tin fleets once paid their harbor-silver.

outcomes.text: A season's harbor-dues in a barnacled chest.
Ingots of tin stacked like firewood, ready coin to any smith.
The syndicate's reserve, hidden against a raid that came from the wrong direction.

sites.name: Oath-Breakers' Camp
sites.text: Warriors cast out for breaking a chieftain's oath, camped sullen at the forest's edge.

outcomes.text: A band of the outcasts swears a new oath — to you.
The whole camp kneels; shamed men fight hard for a second chance.
The camp lies empty, but their war-takings were left where they buried them.

sites.name: Circle of Standing Stones
sites.text: Grey stones raised by no people anyone remembers, on a plain that hums with wind.

outcomes.text: Offerings lie in the turf at every stone's foot — old bronze, old silver.
A night inside the circle leaves the soldiers quiet, and strangely sure of their footing.
Under the altar stone, a king's burial hoard.
